# Ansible Conventions For nomad-infra

- Keep `inventory.ini` out of manual edits. It is generated by Terraform from `terraform/aws/compute.tf`.
- Prefer role-based changes in `ansible/roles/*` over ad-hoc one-off tasks in top-level playbooks.
- Keep `site.yaml` as the main orchestration entry point. Consul playbooks run before Nomad playbooks. Use individual playbooks (`consul_servers.yaml`, `consul_clients.yaml`, `nomad_servers.yaml`, `nomad_clients.yaml`) for targeted runs.
- If role dependencies change, update `ansible/requirements.yaml` and mention re-running `ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yaml`.
- The Terraform-generated inventory always uses **`[servers]`** and **`[clients]`** as group names. Never reference `nomad_servers`, `consul_servers`, or any other variant in templates or playbooks.
- Always declare `gather_facts: true` explicitly in every playbook. Omitting it can silently break tasks that rely on `ansible_facts`.

## TLS And Certificates

- Preserve the existing TLS flow: generate certs on the Ansible control host via the `tls` role, then distribute to nodes via the `helper` role.
- Do not change certificate file paths or permissions without checking `ansible/roles/tls/README.md`, `ansible/roles/nomad/README.md`, and `ansible/roles/consul/README.md`.
- Never commit generated certificate artifacts under `ansible/.tls/`.

## Role And Variable Patterns

- Reuse role defaults and variables instead of hardcoding values in tasks.
- Keep Nomad versioning centralized in `ansible/roles/nomad/defaults/main.yaml` (`nomad_binary_version`).
- Keep Consul versioning centralized in `ansible/roles/consul/defaults/main.yaml` (`consul_binary_version`).
- Keep server/client behavior toggled by variables (`nomad_server_enabled`, `consul_server_enabled`) rather than duplicating logic.
- All roles include `meta/argument_specs.yaml` — update it when adding or changing role variables.
- New roles must follow the existing structure: `defaults/`, `handlers/`, `meta/`, `tasks/`, `templates/`, `vars/`.
- Use `hashicorp_release` role to install any HashiCorp binary (passes `hashicorp_release_product_name` and `hashicorp_release_product_version`).
- Galaxy `galaxy_tags` entries must be **lowercase alphanumeric only** — no underscores or hyphens. `ansible-lint` (`meta-no-tags` rule) will reject `service_discovery`; use `servicediscovery`.

## HashiCorp Config Validation

- After writing any HashiCorp HCL config template (`nomad.hcl`, `consul.hcl`, etc.), always add a task that runs `<binary> validate <config_dir>` before notifying a restart. This catches broken HCL before it causes a service outage.
- Tag the validate step with `*_validate` (e.g. `consul_validate`, `nomad_validate`) so operators can run `--tags consul_validate` to check config without restarting.
- Example: `command: consul validate {{ consul_config_dir }}`

## Systemd Unit Patterns

- Use `Requires=network-online.target` (not `Wants=`) so the service fails fast when the network is not ready rather than silently starting with no peers.
- When the binary manages its own log file (e.g. Consul `log_file`, Nomad `log_file`), set `StandardOutput=null` and `StandardError=null` in the unit file. Using `StandardOutput=append:` together with a binary-managed log file causes every log line to be written twice.

## Security-Safe Edits

- Treat these as sensitive and never expose them in output or commits: `ansible/ssh_key.pem`, `ansible/tokens/` (all token files), and `ansible/.tls/` (generated TLS files).
- When changing firewall/security guidance, preserve warnings that default SSH exposure, Nomad UI (port 4646), and Consul UI (port 8500) exposure must be restricted for production.
- Keep ACL behavior explicit: this repo defaults to disabled ACLs (`nomad_acl_enabled: false`, `consul_acl_enabled: false`). Use `nomad_acl_bootstrap.yaml` as an optional post-deploy step.
- Add `no_log: true` to any task that renders or transmits secrets (gossip keys, ACL tokens, TLS private keys).

## Validation Expectations

- For playbook changes, run syntax or lint checks when feasible and report what was validated.
- For behavior-impacting role changes, describe expected operator command sequence and link to existing docs instead of duplicating long procedures:
  - `ansible/PLAYBOOKS-README.md`
  - `ansible/README.md`
  - `ansible/README-SECURITY-GROUP.md`
